title: Galaxy Star Projectors: Bedroom Glow-Ups, Done Safely
description: Galaxy star projectors made bedroom glow-ups a TikTok trend. What to look for, how laser safety labels work, and tips for using one safely around children.
h1: Galaxy star projectors: bedroom glow-ups, done safely
intro: A swirling galaxy on the ceiling is one of the easiest room makeovers going. Most projectors use LEDs and small lasers, so a few safety basics matter.
cardText: What to look for, laser labels explained, and using one safely around kids.

sections.html: Most galaxy projectors combine coloured LEDs (for the nebula clouds) with a small laser and a diffraction filter (for the pin-point “stars”). Many add timers, app control and Bluetooth speakers.

Consumer laser products should carry a laser class label. Lower classes are designed to be safe under normal use, but you should never stare into the beam or let young children look into it up close. In the US, the FDA regulates laser products; in the UK and EU, look for clear safety and conformity markings (UKCA/CE) and buy from reputable sellers.

• Choose a known brand with a clear laser class label and instructions.
  • A sleep timer stops it running all night.
  • Check the noise: some have a rotating motor that hums.
  • Avoid unbranded “mystery” projectors from social ads.
